name: default_combine
why: Entry Z-G3. `combine_bodies` demands `operation`, and «union» is by far the most common case: «subtract» and «intersect» are asked for on purpose. Here the default is more dangerous than for the material: getting the direction wrong does not leave a part in the wrong material, it leaves a part with a hole in it that nobody asked for. The two bodies OVERLAP on purpose — the copy is at 60 mm on a part 100 long, so 40 mm of overlap — because «combine_bodies» declares that it FAILS if after the union the bodies are still two: «they usually do not really touch, and I fail instead of confirming a part different from the one you believe». With two distant bodies the union would have failed and the red case would have accused the default instead of the geometry. With the overlap the three outcomes remain unmistakable: union = 80000 (50000+50000-20000), subtract = 30000, intersect = 20000. «succeeded: true» would give all three. And the bodies are indicated with «bodies_uid»: «move_bodies» does not declare it in «required» — it is an either/or between «bodies_uid» and «bodies_ref», which «required» cannot express — but its DESCRIPTION says so plainly. This case learned it by going red on 24/9/2026, and it is the second mistake of the same kind on the same case: written by looking at the schema instead of the description. *The schema says what an operation accepts; the description says what it demands and what it refuses.*

includes: you have not asked for it
